reason: The Ch11 §6 'Baseline (canonical single-host)' bullet attaches the 10 rps arrival rate to the TTFT/SLO claim ('hold TTFT under the SLO ... at 10 rps input-heavy load'), which reads as a capacity claim that one host serves 10 rps at SLO. This is a decision-relevant contradiction between adjacent chapters; the latency/capacity qualifier exists in Ch13 but not at Ch11's point of use. All numbers verified.

reason: Real defect: 'PagedAttention ensures the ~24.1 GB-per-request KV pack fits' states a capacity claim PagedAttention does not affect — 24.1 GB (164 GB total) fits in 640 GB with or without PagedAttention; the mechanism's actual role is allocation efficiency (anti-fragmentation so more packs fit), which is how the book states it in §11.3 ('packed densely and more concurrent requests fit'). The §11.6 bullet conflates the capacity question with the allocation question.
evidence: chapter-11.md §11.6 first bullet: 'pagedattention ensures the ~24.1 gb-per-request kv pack fits; prefix caching is the highest-leverage optimization...'. Same chapter §11.3: 'pagedattention/vllm [s2][1p] allocates kv in fixed blocks shared and evicted like page frames, so the ~24.1 gb per request is packed densely and more concurrent requests fit in the same 640 gb node'. python: 140+24=164 < 640 regardless of PagedAttention.
fix_instruction: File design/manuscript/chapter-11/chapter-11.md, §11.6 'Architecture Consequence', first bullet (Baseline). Replace the clause 'pagedattention ensures the ~24.1 gb-per-request kv pack fits' with 'pagedattention packs the ~24.1 gb-per-request KV densely (fixed-size pages, minimal fragmentation) so more concurrent requests fit in the 640 GB node' — separating the capacity fact (164 GB < 640 GB fits either way) from PagedAttention's allocation-efficiency role, matching §11.3's own wording.
